projects.project_name: BINHI NG KINABUKASAN
projects.description: BINHI NG KINABUKASAN (BINHI) is a scholarship program of the Rotary Club of Naga Heights that provided educational assistance to 100 students of Jose de Villa National High School in Barangay Manguiring, Calabanga, Camarines Sur—a far-flung community with limited access to educational and economic opportunities available in urban areas. By easing the financial burden on students and their families, the project enabled beneficiaries to continue their education with greater confidence and stability. Beyond supporting individual learners, BINHI also strengthened the school’s Parents-Teachers Association (PTA) by improving its financial resources, enabling it to undertake timely and relevant programs and projects for the benefit of the entire school community. Through this initiative, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights invested not only in the education of 100 young people but also in the long-term growth and resilience of a geographically underserved community, creating lasting impact through education.

projects.project_name: SUMMER CLUB TURNOVER AND STRATEGIC PLANNING
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights conducted its Summer Club Turnover and Strategic Planning to formally transition into Rotary Year 2026–2027. The activity brought together club members for fellowship, leadership transition, and strategic planning, providing an opportunity to review the club’s accomplishments, assess its current realities, and establish priorities for the year ahead. As the club celebrated its fifth year, members undertook a timely review and revision of the club’s Vision Statement to ensure it remained responsive to the evolving needs of the community and aligned with the club’s long-term aspirations. The club also launched its BAKAS Presidential Thrust and developed strategic goals, service initiatives, and action plans to guide its programs throughout the Rotary year. The activity strengthened unity, reaffirmed the club’s shared purpose, and established a clear roadmap for sustainable service and lasting community impact.

projects.project_name: TALK ON ETHICAL LEADERSHIP FOR LAW STUDENTS
projects.description: Rotary Club of Naga Heights President Atty. Khristian Damielle Jamer served as the invited resource speaker during the Association of Law Students of the Philippines (ALSP) National Convention, where he delivered a lecture on Ethical Student Leadership for Law Students. The session emphasized integrity, accountability, ethical decision-making, and servant leadership, encouraging future members of the legal profession to cultivate character and professional responsibility from their years in law school. Attended by law student delegates from different law schools across the Philippines, the lecture promoted values-based leadership and reinforced the role of lawyers as servants of justice and nation-building. Through the participation of its Club President, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights advanced Rotary’s commitment to youth development, vocational service, and the formation of ethical leaders who will create lasting impact in their communities and the legal profession.

projects.project_name: UNLOCKING MENTAL WELL-BEING
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights partnered with fellow Rotary clubs in the implementation of Unlocking Mental Well-Being: Tools for Everyday Life, a collaborative mental health advocacy program held on May 31, 2026 at the San Sebastian Parish Hall, San Sebastian Cathedral, Lipa City, Batangas. The activity brought together college students, youth leaders, mental health advocates, and Rotary volunteers for interactive learning sessions, small-group discussions, and practical workshops focused on mental wellness, emotional resilience, stress management, and peer support. Through this multi-club initiative, participants were equipped with practical tools to promote positive mental health and foster supportive communities. The collaboration strengthened Rotary’s commitment to improving health, empowering young people, and building strategic partnerships that create lasting impact beyond club and district boundaries.

projects.project_name: DISKWENTULONG CARD
projects.description: DiskwenTulong Card (DTC) is the flagship resource generation initiative of the Rotary Club of Naga Heights that transforms everyday purchases into opportunities for community service. Through partnerships with local businesses, participating establishments extended exclusive discounts, privileges, and special offers to DTC cardholders, while the sale of the cards generated sustainable funding for the club’s humanitarian programs. The project strengthened collaboration between the business sector and Rotary by promoting local enterprises, encouraging community participation, and demonstrating corporate social responsibility. Proceeds from the initiative support the club’s projects in healthcare, education, legal awareness, livelihood development, youth empowerment, environmental sustainability, and other humanitarian initiatives, creating a sustainable funding model that enables the club to expand its service and create lasting impact in the communities it serves.

projects.project_name: CHARTERING OF THE NCF INTERACT CLUB
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights formally launched the chartering initiative for the NCF Interact Club through a partnership meeting with Naga College Foundation, making it one of the club’s flagship Youth Service project for Rotary Year 2026–2027. The activity brought together Rotary leaders and school administrators to discuss the establishment of an Interact Club that will provide students with opportunities to develop leadership skills, engage in meaningful community service, and embrace the ideals of Service Above Self. Recognizing that sustainable service begins by investing in young people, the initiative was designed to cultivate a new generation of ethical, compassionate, and service-oriented leaders who will continue Rotary’s mission in their schools and communities. By laying the foundation for a vibrant Interact Club, the project ensures continuity of service, strengthens youth engagement, and creates a lasting impact that extends well beyond a single Rotary year.

projects.project_name: LEAD
projects.description: Project LEAD (Leadership, Ethics, Action, and Dedication) was a collaborative youth leadership development program conducted by the Rotary Club of Naga Heights together with its sister clubs for the student leaders of Naga College Foundation – Basic Education Department. The activity equipped participants with the knowledge, values, and skills necessary to become ethical and effective leaders through three learning sessions: Basics of Interact, Ethical Student Leadership, and How to Create Lasting Impact. The program introduced students to Rotary’s youth leadership opportunities, emphasized integrity, accountability, and service as the foundation of leadership, and challenged participants to become changemakers in their schools and communities. Through this multi-club initiative, Rotary strengthened its partnership with educational institutions, promoted youth leadership and character development, and inspired the next generation to embrace Service Above Self while creating lasting impact in their communities.

projects.project_name: LIWANAG SA DILIM: Sustainable Alternative Lighting
projects.description: Project Liwanag sa Dilim was a collaborative humanitarian initiative of the Rotary Club of Naga Heights and its sister clubs that provided 25 SALt Lamps (Sustainable Alternative Lighting) to 25 families in Zone 7, Barangay Harubay, Calabanga, Camarines Sur, an off-grid community that remains beyond the reach of the local electrification program. The SALt Lamps, powered by a simple saline solution of water and salt, offer a safe, sustainable, and environmentally friendly source of light for households without electricity. The project improved the quality of life of beneficiary families by enabling children to study after dark, allowing parents to safely perform household activities at night, and reducing dependence on hazardous kerosene lamps and disposable batteries. Through the combined efforts of the participating Rotary clubs, the initiative demonstrated the power of collaboration in addressing energy poverty, promoting sustainable innovation, and bringing hope and opportunity to underserved communities through lasting service.

projects.project_name: 27TH UP HARONG ACADEMIC FESTIVAL
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights served as one of the Partner Hosts of the 27th UP Harong Academic Festival (AcadFest), an annual regional gathering that brought together hundreds of students from across the Bicol Region for academic competitions, leadership activities, and intellectual discussions. By supporting the festival, the club reaffirmed its commitment to Youth Service by promoting academic excellence, critical thinking, civic engagement, and leadership among young people. The partnership provided students with opportunities to exchange ideas, develop their talents, and cultivate a deeper sense of social responsibility while fostering collaboration among educational institutions and community organizations. Through its participation, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights strengthened its support for youth empowerment and contributed to developing future leaders equipped to create positive and lasting impact in their communities.

projects.project_name: RCNH WEBSITE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights officially launched its club website (rcnagaheights.org) as its primary digital platform for public information, member engagement, and community outreach. The website was developed to enhance the club’s public image by providing accessible information on its service projects, upcoming activities, membership opportunities, partnerships, and organizational updates. It also serves as the official online portal for flagship initiatives, including the DiskwenTulong Card Program, allowing the public to verify card authenticity, explore partner establishments, and learn more about the club’s humanitarian programs. By embracing digital innovation, the project strengthened transparency, improved public accessibility, expanded the club’s reach, and reinforced Rotary’s commitment to effective communication and lasting community impact through technology.

projects.project_name: RUROK: THE RCNH MAGAZINE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights officially launched RUROK, the club’s official magazine, as a platform to document, celebrate, and communicate its service initiatives, partnerships, and achievements. Designed to promote transparency, strengthen public image, and preserve the club’s institutional history, the magazine features stories of impactful projects, member accomplishments, community collaborations, and Rotary values in action. More than a publication, RUROK serves as a lasting record of the club’s journey and a medium for inspiring greater community involvement in Rotary’s mission. Through this initiative, the club enhanced its public outreach, strengthened stakeholder engagement, and reinforced its commitment to sharing stories that encourage service, leadership, and lasting impact.

projects.project_name: 4 IN 1 DISTRICT LEARNING SEMINAR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated in the Rotary District 3820 4-in-1 District Learning Seminar, a comprehensive capacity-building program designed to equip club officers and leaders with the knowledge, tools, and strategies necessary to effectively fulfill their responsibilities during Rotary Year 2026–2027. Through focused learning sessions, the seminar strengthened participants’ understanding of Rotary programs, leadership, club administration, membership, The Rotary Foundation, and other key areas essential to building vibrant and effective clubs. The activity also provided opportunities to learn from District leaders, exchange best practices with fellow Rotarians, and strengthen connections across the District. The Club President successfully completed the prescribed learning program, reinforcing the Rotary Club of Naga Heights’ commitment to continuous leadership development, informed governance, and effective service.

projects.project_name: BRIGADA ESKWELA @ MAHABANG DAHILIG SHS
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported the Brigada Eskwela 2026 in Mahabang Dahilig Senior High School in preparation for the opening of classes. Through the club’s participation and donation, the initiative contributed to creating a safer, cleaner, and more conducive learning environment for students while reinforcing the spirit of volunteerism and shared responsibility among schools, civic organizations, and the community. The project demonstrated Rotary’s commitment to supporting quality education through meaningful partnerships with educational institutions and government agencies. By joining Brigada Eskwela, the club helped strengthen community collaboration and reaffirmed its dedication to empowering young learners by ensuring that schools are ready to provide a safe and welcoming environment for education.

projects.project_name: GOVERNOR'S VISIT
projects.description: The Official Visit of the District Governor to the Rotary Club of Naga Heights served as an opportunity to strengthen fellowship, recognize the club’s accomplishments, and reaffirm its commitment to Rotary’s mission and strategic priorities. During the visit, the club presented its flagship programs, ongoing service initiatives, and organizational goals for Rotary Year 2026–2027, while engaging in meaningful dialogue with the District Governor on opportunities for growth, membership development, public image, and service impact. The visit also marked the successful launch of several key club initiatives, including the DiskwenTulong Card Program, the unveiling of the club’s inaugural issue of RUROK Magazine, and the recognition of partners and supporters who contribute to the club’s humanitarian mission. More than a ceremonial event, the Governor’s Visit inspired members to pursue excellence in service, strengthen collaboration, and continue creating lasting impact in the communities they serve.

projects.project_name: RUROK: THE RCNH MAGAZINE JUNE 2026 ISSUE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights marked a significant milestone in its institutional development with the official launch of RUROK, the club's monthly bulletin, through the publication of its inaugural June 2026 issue. Carrying the tagline “Stories of Service, Stories of Leadership, Stories of Impact,” the publication was established as a dedicated platform for documenting the club's accomplishments, promoting Rotary education, recognizing member contributions, strengthening public image, and preserving its organizational history. Inspired by the Filipino word “rurok,” meaning the highest point or summit, the magazine symbolizes the club's continuing pursuit of excellence in leadership, fellowship, and humanitarian service. The inaugural issue introduced BAKAS, the Presidential Thrust for Rotary Year 2026–2027, outlining its five pillars: Buhay at Kalusugan, Aral at Karunungan, Katarungan at Kapayapaan, Angat na Kabuhayan, and Serbisyo at Kapaligirang Pangmatagalan. It documented important organizational milestones, including the club's Summer Turnover and Strategic Planning, participation in the District 3820 Handover and Mass Induction Ceremonies, and the Binhi ng Kinabukasan Scholarship Awarding Program, through which 100 scholarship vouchers were extended to deserving students of Jose de Villa National High School. The publication also highlighted youth leadership initiatives, including the club's efforts toward establishing the Naga College Foundation Interact Club and President KD Jamer's presentation on Ethical Student Leadership at the National Convention of Filipino Law Students. To strengthen Rotary education, the issue featured articles on Rotary founder Paul P. Harris, the organization's history, the Four-Way Test, and the contributions of healthcare professionals to polio eradication. Its inaugural ORAGON of the Month feature recognized Charter President Atty. Ghiel “Oying” Rosales for his contributions to Rotary, the legal profession, and public service. The publication also introduced the club's leadership team and highlighted its public image initiatives, including the establishment of its official website. Beyond serving as a monthly record of activities, RUROK was envisioned as a living chronicle of the club's collective journey, providing a sustainable medium for institutional knowledge-sharing, organizational transparency, member recognition, and stakeholder engagement. Through the successful publication of its maiden issue, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights established a continuing communication platform that celebrates service, preserves institutional memory, strengthens the public's understanding of Rotary, and inspires present and future generations to embrace Service Above Self and Create Lasting Impact.

projects.project_name: RUROK: THE RCNH MAGAZINE JULY 2026 ISSUE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights continued strengthening its institutional communications and public image through the publication of the second issue of RUROK, the club's official monthly bulletin, for July 2026. Carrying the theme “Stories of Service, Stories of Leadership, Stories of Impact,” the publication documented the club's activities during the first full month of Rotary Year 2026–2027, highlighting its commitment to transforming the BAKAS Presidential Thrust into meaningful community action. The issue featured the club's initiatives in Youth Service, particularly the proposed establishment of the Naga College Foundation Interact Club and the implementation of Project LEAD (Leadership, Ethics, Action, and Dedication), a collaborative leadership development program undertaken with partner Rotary clubs. It also documented the Liwanag sa Dilim Project, through which 25 saltwater-powered lamps were distributed to families in an off-grid community in Barangay Harubay, Calabanga, Camarines Sur. Additional features included the club's regular meetings, inter-club engagements, the development of the DiskwenTulong Card Program, and the presentation of the club's officers for the Rotary year. The publication also introduced the ORAGON of the Month feature, recognizing Past President Jason Bagadiong for his professional accomplishments and contributions to Rotary, alongside articles highlighting Rotary International's humanitarian initiatives and the achievements of club members. Beyond documenting accomplishments, RUROK served as an institutional platform for promoting transparency, strengthening member engagement, recognizing individual contributions, and preserving the club's organizational history. Through its second issue, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to purposeful communication, effective public image development, and inspiring greater participation in Rotary's mission of Service Above Self and Creating Lasting Impact.

projects.project_name: RUROK: THE RCNH MAGAZINE AUGUST 2026 ISSUE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights sustained its commitment to institutional documentation, public image development, and stakeholder engagement through the publication of the third issue of RUROK, its official monthly bulletin, for August 2026. Building upon the foundations established in its previous editions, the publication highlighted a month characterized by organizational development, strategic partnerships, community empowerment, and sustainable service initiatives under the club's BAKAS Presidential Thrust. Among its major features was the 6th District Governor's Visit, which showcased the club's leadership transition, service accomplishments, organizational priorities, and the official launch of the DiskwenTulong Card, its flagship resource-generation initiative designed to connect consumer benefits with sustainable funding for community service projects. The issue also documented the establishment of the Rotary Community Corps of Sibobo in Calabanga, Camarines Sur, the club's participation as Platinum Sponsor and Co-Project Host of the PANDA environmental conservation initiative, and its support as an Elite Sponsor and Partner Host of the 27th UP Harong Academic Festival. Particular emphasis was given to membership and professional development through the Area 4 Membership Orientation Seminar and the inaugural session of ANGAT: The RCNH Capacity Building Series. The publication further featured Past President Brian Kierby Felipe as ORAGON of the Month, recognized the academic achievement of Club Adviser Dr. Ryan Bastareche, and provided updates on Rotary International, District 3820, and the club's expanding DiskwenTulong Card partner network. Through comprehensive documentation and purposeful storytelling, RUROK served as a platform for recognizing partnerships, preserving institutional milestones, promoting Rotary education, and communicating the club's growing contributions to community development. The third issue reinforced the Rotary Club of Naga Heights' commitment to organizational transparency, meaningful public engagement, and the promotion of service initiatives designed to create positive and lasting impact.

projects.project_name: DISKUBROTARY: ROTARY'S PLAN OF ACTION
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights launched DISKUBROTARY, an institutionalized Rotary education initiative integrated into the club's regular meetings, designed to deepen members' understanding of Rotary International, strengthen organizational engagement, and cultivate a more informed and service-oriented membership. Each session focuses on a specific Rotary-related topic, providing members with opportunities for continuous learning, meaningful discussions, and a greater appreciation of Rotary's principles, priorities, programs, and global humanitarian mission. The inaugural session introduced Rotary's Action Plan, the organization's strategic framework built upon four priorities: Increase Our Impact, Expand Our Reach, Enhance Participant Engagement, and Increase Our Ability to Adapt. Through this learning session, members were oriented on how these priorities guide Rotary clubs in designing meaningful service projects, strengthening membership participation, building sustainable partnerships, and responding effectively to evolving community needs. The discussion also emphasized the importance of aligning the club's initiatives and long-term objectives with Rotary International's strategic direction to maximize organizational effectiveness and community impact. Beyond imparting institutional knowledge, DISKUBROTARY seeks to foster a culture of lifelong learning, shared leadership, and active participation by making Rotary education a consistent component of the club's regular activities. Through this continuing initiative, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to developing knowledgeable and engaged Rotarians who understand not only the responsibilities of membership but also the deeper purpose of their service. By investing in Rotary education, the club aims to strengthen its institutional foundations, enhance the quality and sustainability of its programs, and empower its members to translate Rotary's ideals into meaningful action that creates lasting impact.

projects.project_name: ESTABLISHMENT OF RCC SIBOBO @ CALABANGA, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights initiated the establishment of the Rotary Community Corps (RCC) of Sibobo in Barangay Sibobo, Calabanga, Camarines Sur, as part of its commitment to promoting sustainable livelihood, grassroots empowerment, and community economic development. On August 17, 2026, the club conducted an engagement meeting with barangay officials and community leaders, culminating in the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) formalizing the partnership for the establishment of the RCC and the proposed development of a community-based Local Economic Enterprise (LEE). The initiative seeks to organize and empower local residents as active partners in identifying community needs, developing livelihood opportunities, and implementing sustainable economic programs. Through the proposed enterprise, the club envisions strengthening local capacities, encouraging community participation, and creating opportunities for long-term economic self-sufficiency. Aligned with Rotary's focus on Community Economic Development and the Angat na Kabuhayan pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the project represents a strategic shift from short-term assistance toward community-led development. By laying the groundwork for an organized and economically empowered community, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its dedication to fostering self-reliance, strengthening local partnerships, and creating positive and lasting impact for the people of Sibobo.

projects.project_name: PANDA PROJECT: PROTECTING AREAS, NURTURING DIVERSITY AND AWARENESS @ PANICUASON, NAGA CITY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated as a Platinum Sponsor and Co-Project Host of the PANDA Project (Protecting Areas, Nurturing Diversity and Awareness), a tree-planting and environmental awareness initiative spearheaded by the Rotaract Club of Naga, Inc., in Barangay Panicuason, Naga City, at the foot of Mount Isarog. The project brought together Rotarians, Rotaractors, community partners, and volunteers in a collaborative effort to promote environmental conservation, restore natural ecosystems, and strengthen public awareness of the importance of protecting biodiversity. Through the planting of tree seedlings, the initiative sought to contribute to reforestation efforts, preserve ecological balance, and encourage long-term environmental stewardship among participating organizations and local communities. Beyond the tree-planting activity, the project emphasized collective responsibility in safeguarding natural resources and fostering a culture of environmental consciousness. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Protecting the Environment and the Serbisyo at Kapaligirang Pangmatagalan pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to sustainable environmental action through meaningful partnerships. By supporting this initiative, the club contributed to efforts to protect the natural heritage of Mount Isarog and promote a healthier, greener, and more resilient environment for present and future generations.

projects.project_name: AREA 4 MEMBERSHIPORIENTATION SEMINAR @ VILLA GAITE, NABUA, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated in the Area 4 Membership Orientation Seminar held on August 22, 2026, at Villa Gaite, Baao, Camarines Sur, as part of its continuing commitment to membership development, leadership enhancement, and Rotary education. Representing the club were Service Impact President KD Jamer, Club Secretary and President-Elect Kathleen Felipe, and Club Administration and Vocational Service Chair Raymar Bron. Hosted by the Rotary Club of Legazpi Central, the seminar brought together Rotarians from across Area 4 to deepen their understanding of Rotary's principles, organizational structure, membership responsibilities, and opportunities for meaningful service. Through informative discussions and knowledge-sharing sessions facilitated by District Governor Eric Santos, district officers, and resource speakers, participants gained valuable insights into strengthening member engagement, promoting retention, and cultivating effective club leadership. The activity also provided opportunities for fellowship, collaboration, and the exchange of best practices among participating Rotary clubs. By investing in the continuing education and professional development of its members, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced its commitment to building a knowledgeable, motivated, and service-oriented membership capable of sustaining impactful programs and advancing Rotary's mission. The club's participation underscored its recognition that strong and engaged members are essential to strengthening the organization, expanding its capacity to serve, and creating lasting impact in the communities it supports.

projects.project_name: ANGAT: THE RCNH CAPACITY BUILDING SERIES - BUILDING A BETTER YOU
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights launched ANGAT: The RCNH Capacity Building Series, a continuing learning and development initiative designed to enhance the personal, professional, and leadership competencies of its members through knowledge-sharing sessions facilitated by fellow Rotarians and invited resource speakers. The inaugural session, entitled “Building a Better YOU,” was conducted during the club's 5th Regular Meeting at Dy Viajero Hotel in Naga City and featured Rtn. Florence Rañola, who shared valuable insights and practical perspectives drawn from her studies at the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising in San Francisco, California. The session emphasized the importance of personal development, self-improvement, professional presentation, and cultivating a positive and confident personal image as essential elements of individual growth and effective interpersonal engagement. Through this initiative, the club sought to maximize the diverse educational backgrounds, professional experiences, and specialized expertise of its members by creating a platform for continuous learning, mentorship, and the exchange of practical knowledge. Beyond strengthening individual competencies, ANGAT aims to encourage a culture of lifelong learning, professional excellence, and mutual empowerment within the organization, recognizing that personal growth contributes to stronger leadership, more meaningful fellowship, and greater effectiveness in community service. The activity also demonstrated Rotary's unique capacity to bring together professionals from different fields who can enrich one another through the sharing of knowledge, experiences, and skills. Aligned with Rotary's commitment to membership development and professional growth, the inaugural ANGAT session reinforced the Rotary Club of Naga Heights' dedication to investing in its members as the foundation of a strong, dynamic, and sustainable service organization. By institutionalizing opportunities for capacity building and self-development, the club seeks to nurture capable, confident, and purpose-driven Rotarians who are better equipped to lead, collaborate, and create lasting impact in their professions and communities.

projects.project_name: DISKUBROTARY: MEMBERSHIP
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights continued its DISKUBROTARY learning series through its second session, which focused on Rotary Membership as a fundamental pillar of organizational growth, sustainability, and effective community service. Conducted as part of the club's regular meeting, the session aimed to deepen members' understanding of the meaning, privileges, responsibilities, and opportunities associated with being a Rotarian, while emphasizing the importance of building a strong, diverse, inclusive, and actively engaged membership. The discussion highlighted the significance of member recruitment, retention, engagement, and professional fellowship in strengthening the club's institutional capacity and ensuring the continuity of its humanitarian initiatives. Particular emphasis was placed on the value of cultivating a positive club experience, fostering meaningful relationships among members, recognizing individual talents and professional expertise, and creating opportunities for every Rotarian to contribute to the organization's shared mission. The session also reinforced the principle that Rotary membership extends beyond attendance at meetings or participation in occasional activities, representing a continuing commitment to ethical leadership, personal development, fellowship, and Service Above Self. Aligned with Rotary's Action Plan priorities of Expanding Our Reach and Enhancing Participant Engagement, the learning activity encouraged members to take an active role in strengthening the club's membership culture and inspiring others to become part of Rotary's global network of service-minded individuals. Through DISKUBROTARY Session 2, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to nurturing an informed, motivated, and purpose-driven membership, recognizing that the sustainability of its programs and the achievement of lasting community impact ultimately depend on the dedication, unity, and active participation of its members.

projects.project_name: RUROK: THE RCNH MAGAZINE SEPTEMBER 2026 ISSUE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights further strengthened its institutional communications and public image initiatives through the publication of the fourth issue of RUROK, its official monthly bulletin, for September 2026. Continuing its commitment to documenting meaningful service, leadership, and organizational development, the publication highlighted the club's growing efforts to translate its BAKAS Presidential Thrust into sustainable community programs and lasting partnerships. The issue prominently featured PANDA Project 2.0, an environmental conservation initiative involving bamboo and mangrove planting activities undertaken with the Rotaract Club of Naga, Inc. and partner organizations, demonstrating the club's continuing commitment to protecting biodiversity and strengthening environmental resilience. It also documented the advancement of the Rotary Community Corps of Sibobo through a technical training program on African catfish grow-out culture facilitated by the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, marking a significant step toward developing a community-managed livelihood enterprise. The publication featured the club's 6th Regular Meeting, which highlighted ongoing service initiatives, proposed collaborative projects, organizational developments, and updates on the DiskwenTulong Card Program and The Rotary Foundation. Its ORAGON of the Month feature recognized Past President Carlo Richardo Sierra, highlighting his professional expertise in information and communications technology and his contributions to sustainable, technology-driven community service. The issue also celebrated the commissioning of Club President Atty. Khristian Damielle A. Jamer as an Electronic Notary Public and featured articles on Rotary International's humanitarian initiatives and global leadership developments. Beyond serving as a record of organizational accomplishments, RUROK promoted institutional continuity, strengthened member recognition, encouraged collaboration, and communicated Rotary's values to a broader audience. Through its fourth issue, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced its commitment to effective public image development, transparent communication, and preserving the collective achievements of its members and partners as part of its continuing journey toward Creating Lasting Impact.

projects.project_name: 5TH LEG OF THE DISTRICT GOLF TOURNAMENT
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported the spirit of inter-club fellowship, professional networking, and service-oriented fundraising through the 5th Leg of the District Golf Tournament, hosted by the Rotary Club of Batangas Malarayat on September 4, 2026. The tournament brought together Rotarians, golf enthusiasts, business professionals, sponsors, and community partners in an activity that combined sportsmanship, camaraderie, and a shared commitment to humanitarian service. Beyond providing opportunities for friendly competition and professional interaction, the event served as a fundraising platform intended to generate resources for meaningful community service initiatives and charitable programs. Through the collective participation and generosity of golfers, sponsors, and supporters, the tournament demonstrated how recreational activities and professional networks can be mobilized to advance social responsibility and strengthen the capacity of Rotary clubs to serve their communities. The initiative also reinforced the importance of fellowship, collaboration, and mutual support among Rotary clubs, fostering relationships that can lead to future partnerships and joint service undertakings. Aligned with Rotary's commitment to Vocational Service, the activity highlighted the value of bringing together individuals from diverse professional backgrounds to contribute their resources, relationships, and expertise toward common humanitarian objectives. By recognizing the connection between professional fellowship and community engagement, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its support for collaborative fundraising initiatives that strengthen Rotary's network of service-minded individuals, encourage generosity, and create opportunities for positive and lasting impact beyond the golf course.

projects.project_name: PANDA PROJECT 2.0: PROTECTING AREAS, NURTURING DIVERSITY AND AWARENESS @ BONGALON, BULA, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights continued its commitment to environmental conservation and sustainability by participating as a Platinum Sponsor of PANDA Project 2.0 (Protecting Areas, Nurturing Diversity and Awareness), an environmental initiative undertaken in partnership with the Rotaract Club of Naga, Inc. The project formed part of the Environment Conservation and Sustainability Program spearheaded by the Baao Parish Multi-Purpose Cooperative (BPMPCO), in collaboration with DENR-CENRO Goa, Barangay Bongalon, CLIMBS Community Affairs, and other participating organizations. Building upon the success of the initial PANDA Project, the initiative featured two complementary environmental activities involving the planting of bamboo seedlings and mangrove propagules to promote ecological restoration, biodiversity conservation, and climate resilience. The bamboo-planting activity sought to strengthen vegetation cover, support soil conservation, and contribute to sustainable land management, while the mangrove-planting activity aimed to help protect coastal ecosystems, reduce shoreline erosion, and enhance the natural defenses of coastal communities against environmental hazards. Through its sponsorship and active participation, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported a collaborative approach to environmental stewardship that brought together civic organizations, government agencies, and community volunteers in protecting natural resources. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Protecting the Environment and the \*Serbisyo at Kapaligirang Pangmatagalan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the project reinforced the importance of sustained environmental action and interorganizational partnerships. By supporting conservation efforts across upland and coastal ecosystems, the club contributed to building healthier, more resilient, and environmentally sustainable communities for present and future generations.

projects.project_name: DISKUBROTARY: BASIC EDUCATION & LITERACY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights continued its DISKUBROTARY learning series through its third session, which focused on Basic Education and Literacy, one of Rotary International's seven areas of focus and a fundamental component of sustainable community development. Conducted as part of the club's regular meeting, the session aimed to deepen members' understanding of Rotary's commitment to improving access to quality education, strengthening literacy skills, and creating meaningful learning opportunities for children, youth, and adults, particularly those belonging to underserved and disadvantaged communities. The discussion highlighted the importance of foundational literacy and numeracy, teacher support, educational resources, and community involvement in addressing barriers to learning and promoting educational equity. Members were also introduced to the various ways Rotary clubs can contribute to educational development through school-based outreach programs, reading and literacy initiatives, provision of learning materials, support for educators, and partnerships with educational institutions and local communities. Beyond familiarizing members with Rotary's educational priorities, the session emphasized the importance of designing sustainable, needs-based service projects that address underlying educational challenges rather than merely providing short-term assistance. The discussion further encouraged members to recognize education as a powerful instrument for breaking cycles of poverty, expanding economic opportunities, and empowering individuals to participate meaningfully in society. Through DISKUBROTARY Session 3, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced its commitment to continuous Rotary education and strengthened its members' capacity to conceptualize and implement impactful initiatives aligned with Basic Education and Literacy. By fostering a deeper appreciation of education as a foundation for individual empowerment and community progress, the club reaffirmed its dedication to developing knowledgeable Rotarians capable of translating Rotary's humanitarian priorities into purposeful service and creating lasting impact through education.

projects.project_name: PUNO NG PAG-ASA
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported the Puno ng Pag-asa: Sponsor-a-Tree Project, an environmental conservation and reforestation initiative spearheaded by the Rotary Club of Lipa West, held on September 12, 2026, in Barangay Malitlit, Lipa City, Batangas. The project brought together Rotarians, Rotaractors, donors, families, community volunteers, and partner organizations in a collective effort to promote environmental sustainability, strengthen ecological resilience, and encourage public participation in protecting natural resources. Initially targeting the planting of 1,000 tree seedlings, the initiative successfully exceeded its original goal through the combined generosity and participation of its supporters, resulting in the planting of 1,650 seedlings. The activity sought to contribute to the restoration of vegetation cover, improvement of environmental conditions, conservation of biodiversity, and promotion of long-term ecological sustainability. Beyond the physical act of planting trees, the project emphasized the importance of shared environmental responsibility, volunteerism, and sustained community involvement in addressing environmental challenges. Through its support for this inter-club initiative, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced the value of collaboration among Rotary clubs and community stakeholders in undertaking environmental programs that extend beyond geographical and district boundaries. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Protecting the Environment and the \*Serbisyo at Kapaligirang Pangmatagalan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the initiative demonstrated how collective action and community partnerships can transform modest individual contributions into meaningful environmental outcomes. By supporting the successful planting of 1,650 tree seedlings, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to environmental stewardship, sustainable community development, and the creation of a greener, healthier, and more resilient environment for present and future generations.

projects.project_name: LINIG PARA KAY INA CLEAN UP DRIVE
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights served as a partner organization in “Linig Para Ki Inâ,” a community clean-up and environmental conservation initiative spearheaded by JCI Naga Cariñosa and RMN DWNX Naga on September 15, 2026, in preparation for the annual Fluvial Procession honoring Our Lady of Peñafrancia. The project brought together civic organizations, government agencies, media practitioners, and community volunteers in a collective effort to clean the Basilica Landing Area, locally known as the Dagsaan, its surrounding areas, and portions of the Naga River, a significant waterway in Bicol's religious and cultural heritage. Through its partnership and financial contribution, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported the implementation of the initiative, which sought to reduce waste accumulation, preserve the cleanliness of public spaces, protect the river ecosystem, and promote a safer and more environmentally responsible celebration for thousands of devotees and pilgrims. The activity was undertaken in collaboration with the City Government of Naga, particularly the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, City Environment and Natural Resources Office, and City Tourism Office, alongside the Archdiocese of Caceres and participating Junior Chamber International chapters from across the Bicol Region. Beyond preparing the procession route for the religious festivities, the project promoted environmental awareness, responsible waste management, volunteerism, and collective accountability in protecting natural resources and shared community spaces. The partnership demonstrated the importance of cooperation among civic organizations, local government institutions, and community stakeholders in addressing environmental concerns while preserving cherished cultural and religious traditions. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Protecting the Environment and the \*Serbisyo at Kapaligirang Pangmatagalan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the initiative reinforced the Rotary Club of Naga Heights' commitment to supporting sustainable environmental practices and meaningful community partnerships. Through its involvement, the club contributed to safeguarding the environmental integrity of the Naga River, promoting civic responsibility, and creating lasting impact through collective service to both the community and the environment.

projects.project_name: BAD FUN RUN
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported the B.A.D. (Batangueño Ayaw sa Droga) Fun Run for a Cause 2026, a community-based health advocacy and drug prevention initiative jointly organized by the Rotary Club of Downtown Batangas City and the Rotary Club of Downtown Taysan on September 26, 2026, along Bypass Road in Barangay Sampaga, Batangas City. The event brought together Rotarians, runners, volunteers, sponsors, and community stakeholders in a collective effort to raise public awareness about the dangers of illegal drug use, promote healthy lifestyles, and encourage greater community involvement in substance abuse prevention. Through a recreational running activity anchored on the advocacy “Say Yes to Life and No to Drugs,” the project sought to reinforce positive health behaviors, encourage physical fitness, and inspire individuals, particularly young people, to make responsible choices that contribute to their personal well-being and the safety of their communities. Beyond promoting physical activity, the initiative emphasized the importance of education, prevention, and collective responsibility in addressing the harmful effects of drug abuse on individuals, families, and society. The collaboration between Rotary clubs demonstrated the value of inter-club partnerships in strengthening public health advocacy and mobilizing community participation in initiatives that promote safer and healthier environments. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Disease Prevention and Treatment and the \*Buhay at Kalusugan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the project reinforced the Rotary Club of Naga Heights' commitment to supporting preventive health programs and community-based awareness campaigns. Through its support for this initiative, the club contributed to advancing the shared goal of building healthier, more informed, and drug-free communities while strengthening solidarity among Rotary clubs in creating positive and lasting impact.

projects.project_name: CATFISH GROW OUT CULTURE TRAINING OF RCC SIBOBO, CALABANGA, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights advanced its community economic development initiative in Barangay Sibobo, Calabanga, Camarines Sur, through the conduct of a Catfish Grow-Out Culture Training for members of the newly established Rotary Community Corps (RCC) of Sibobo. Building upon the Memorandum of Agreement previously executed between the club and the Barangay Local Government Unit of Sibobo, the activity marked an important step toward transforming the community partnership into a sustainable livelihood enterprise. Facilitated by the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), the training equipped RCC members, composed of barangay tanods and barangay aides, with essential technical knowledge and practical skills in the cultivation and grow-out management of African catfish. The initiative represents the first phase of the community-based Local Economic Enterprise envisioned under the partnership, with catfish farming identified as an initial livelihood opportunity capable of supporting income generation and local economic participation. Rather than providing temporary assistance, the project emphasized skills development, capacity building, and community ownership as foundations for long-term economic self-sufficiency. Through collaboration among the Rotary Club of Naga Heights, BFAR, and the Barangay Government of Sibobo, the activity demonstrated the value of combining institutional support, technical expertise, and grassroots participation in developing sustainable livelihood opportunities. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Community Economic Development and the \*Angat na Kabuhayan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the project reinforced the club's commitment to empowering communities with the knowledge, resources, and opportunities necessary to build their own economic future. By investing in the capabilities of RCC Sibobo members, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights laid the groundwork for a community-managed enterprise intended to promote economic independence, strengthen local livelihoods, and create lasting impact.

projects.project_name: PROJECT HABI @ TINANQUIHAN PRIMARY SCHOOL, LIBMANAN, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights, in collaboration with partner organizations and volunteer nurses, implemented Project HABI (Harnessing Arts, Books, and Imagination) on September 29, 2026, at Tinanquihan Primary School in Libmanan, Camarines Sur, as part of its commitment to advancing basic education, literacy, and holistic child development. The initiative benefited pupils from Grades 1 to 3 through a series of interactive educational and creative activities designed to nurture imagination, strengthen foundational literacy skills, and encourage active participation in learning. The program featured an engaging storytelling session that promoted reading comprehension, listening skills, and appreciation for literature, alongside the “Make Me a Hero” artwork activity, which provided children with an opportunity to express their creativity, aspirations, and understanding of positive values through art. To further support their educational needs, the project also facilitated the distribution of school supplies and coloring books, providing learners with materials that could enhance their classroom participation and creative development. Beyond the provision of educational resources, Project HABI sought to create an inclusive and encouraging learning environment where young children could discover their talents, develop self-confidence, and cultivate a positive attitude toward education. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Basic Education and Literacy, the initiative demonstrated the importance of collaborative community engagement in addressing the developmental and educational needs of young learners. Through Project HABI, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to empowering children through accessible learning opportunities, fostering creativity and intellectual curiosity, and helping build a stronger educational foundation for the next generation.

projects.project_name: PROJECT NGITI @ TINANQUIHAN PRIMARY SCHOOL, LIBMANAN, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights, in collaboration with partner organizations and volunteer nurses, conducted Project NGITI (Nurturing Good Habits, Teaching the Importance of Oral Health) on September 29, 2026, at Tinanquihan Primary School in Libmanan, Camarines Sur, as part of its continuing commitment to promoting preventive healthcare, oral hygiene, and the overall well-being of young learners. The initiative provided elementary pupils with an interactive oral health education session designed to raise awareness of the importance of proper dental care and the prevention of common oral health problems, particularly tooth decay and gum disease. Through engaging discussions and practical toothbrushing demonstrations facilitated by volunteer nurses, the children learned essential brushing techniques and the importance of developing consistent oral hygiene habits from an early age. The activity emphasized the relationship between oral health and general well-being, encouraging pupils to take an active role in maintaining healthy teeth and gums through simple, everyday preventive practices. Beyond promoting dental hygiene, Project NGITI sought to instill personal responsibility, self-care, and health consciousness among young learners while demonstrating the importance of early intervention in preventing avoidable oral health conditions. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Disease Prevention and Treatment, the project highlighted the value of partnerships among civic organizations, healthcare volunteers, and educational institutions in bringing practical health education closer to underserved school communities. Through Project NGITI, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to empowering children with essential health knowledge, nurturing lifelong preventive care practices, and contributing to healthier, more confident, and more resilient future generations.

projects.project_name: PROJECT WASH @ TINANQUIHAN PRIMARY SCHOOL, LIBMANAN, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights, in collaboration with partner organizations and volunteer nurses, conducted Project WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) at Tinanquihan Primary School in Libmanan, Camarines Sur, as part of its commitment to promoting disease prevention, personal hygiene, and the health and well-being of young learners. The initiative benefited pupils from Grades 1 to 3 through an interactive health education session focused on proper handwashing techniques and the importance of maintaining good hygiene practices in everyday life. Led by volunteer nurses, the activity featured practical handwashing demonstrations designed to equip children with essential knowledge and habits that can help prevent the transmission of communicable diseases and reduce the risk of common infections. Through age-appropriate instruction and hands-on participation, the project sought to encourage learners to adopt regular handwashing practices and develop a greater awareness of their personal responsibility in maintaining a clean and healthy environment. Beyond imparting basic hygiene knowledge, Project WASH emphasized the importance of preventive healthcare and early health education in promoting healthier school communities. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Disease Prevention and Treatment, the initiative demonstrated the value of collaboration among civic organizations, healthcare volunteers, and educational institutions in addressing the health needs of children. Through Project WASH, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to empowering young learners with practical health knowledge, fostering lifelong hygiene habits, and contributing to safer, healthier, and more resilient communities.

projects.project_name: PROMDI: PHILIPPINE ROTARY MULTI-DISTRICT INTERACTION @ ALABANG, MANDALUYONG
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated in the Philippine Rotary Multi-District Interaction (PROMDI) held on October 3, 2026, at The Bellevue Hotel in Alabang, Muntinlupa City, with the club represented by Service Impact President KD Jamer. Recognized as one of the largest gatherings of Filipino Rotarians in 2026, the event brought together members and leaders from Rotary International Districts 3780, 3820, 3830, and 3860 to strengthen fellowship, foster inter-district cooperation, and promote meaningful collaboration among Rotary clubs across the Philippines. The gathering provided a valuable platform for exchanging ideas, sharing experiences and best practices, exploring potential service partnerships, and establishing professional and personal connections beyond district boundaries. Through its participation, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights sought to expand its network of Rotary partners, gain insights into innovative approaches to club development and community service, and identify opportunities for collaborative initiatives capable of extending the reach and effectiveness of its programs. The event also reinforced the importance of unity, shared leadership, and collective action in advancing Rotary's mission of service to humanity. By actively engaging with fellow Rotarians from different districts, the club demonstrated its commitment to strengthening its institutional relationships and building partnerships that can support its long-term service objectives. Aligned with the club's BAKAS thrust and Rotary's commitment to Service Above Self, RCNH's participation in PROMDI underscored its recognition that meaningful connections and sustained collaboration are essential to expanding service opportunities, strengthening Rotary fellowship, and creating lasting impact in communities across the country.

projects.project_name: RED START 2026: THE RED SPARTAN ROTARACT CLUB ORSEM, BATANGAS STATE UNIVERSITY, LIPA, BATANGAS
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights extended its commitment to youth empowerment, leadership development, and the advancement of Rotary's ideals through its participation in RED START 2026, the orientation seminar of the newly chartered Red Spartan Rotaract Club of Batangas State University, held on October 4, 2026, in Lipa City, Batangas. Representing the club as one of the invited resource speakers, Service Impact President KD Jamer delivered an inspirational and educational presentation to the 66 charter members of the Red Spartan Rotaract Club, emphasizing the importance of cultivating a lifelong commitment to service, strengthening organizational identity, and embracing the responsibilities of Rotary membership. His discussion introduced the young Rotaractors to Rotary International's global network, its guiding principle of Service Above Self, and its areas of focus, including peacebuilding, disease prevention, water and sanitation, maternal and child health, basic education, community economic development, environmental protection, and the global campaign to eradicate polio. Beyond familiarizing participants with Rotary's humanitarian mission, the presentation encouraged them to recognize service not merely as an occasional activity but as a personal value and enduring responsibility that shapes their character and leadership. The seminar also highlighted the importance of fellowship, shared purpose, and sustained member engagement in building a resilient and impactful service organization. Through its involvement, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights contributed to the orientation and development of emerging youth leaders while strengthening its connections with the wider Rotaract community beyond its home district. Aligned with Rotary's commitment to Youth Service, the initiative reaffirmed the club's dedication to mentoring the next generation of service-oriented leaders, nurturing meaningful youth participation in community development, and inspiring young people to become active agents of positive and lasting change.

projects.project_name: DISKUBROTARY: END POLIO
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights continued its DISKUBROTARY learning series through its fourth session, which focused on End Polio Now, Rotary International's flagship humanitarian campaign and one of the most significant global public health initiatives supported by the organization. Conducted as part of the club's regular meeting, the session aimed to deepen members' understanding of poliomyelitis, its devastating effects on children, and Rotary's decades-long commitment to eradicating the disease worldwide. The discussion highlighted Rotary's pioneering involvement in polio eradication beginning with its PolioPlus program in 1985, its role as a founding partner of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative in 1988, and the remarkable progress achieved through sustained vaccination campaigns, disease surveillance, international cooperation, and community mobilization. Members were oriented on the historic reduction in global wild poliovirus cases, the Philippines' certification as polio-free in 2000, and the continuing challenges in Afghanistan and Pakistan, the remaining countries where wild poliovirus transmission remains endemic. The session also emphasized the importance of Rotary's PolioPlus Fund, the contributions of The Rotary Foundation, and the collective efforts of Rotarians, governments, healthcare workers, and international partners in sustaining the global eradication campaign. Beyond providing historical and technical knowledge, the learning activity encouraged members to recognize their individual responsibilities in advancing the End Polio Now advocacy through public awareness, fundraising, volunteerism, and community engagement. Particular emphasis was placed on the principle that the fight against polio cannot end until transmission is interrupted worldwide, as continued circulation of the virus anywhere poses a potential threat to children everywhere. Through DISKUBROTARY Session 4, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights strengthened its members' appreciation of Rotary's enduring humanitarian legacy and reinforced their commitment to participating actively in the final stages of global polio eradication. By connecting Rotary education with one of the organization's most defining causes, the club reaffirmed its dedication to developing informed and engaged Rotarians who are prepared to champion disease prevention, mobilize community support, and contribute to the historic goal of making polio the second human disease eradicated worldwide.

projects.project_name: END POLIO BILLBOARD @ PANGANIBAN DRIVE, NAGA CITY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights launched a month-long End Polio Billboard Advocacy Campaign along Panganiban Drive, Naga City, from October 10 to November 10, 2026, as part of its continuing commitment to Rotary International's global mission of eradicating poliomyelitis. Bearing the powerful message “END POLIO FOR GOOD,” the billboard served as a highly visible public awareness platform designed to educate motorists, pedestrians, and the wider community about the continuing threat of polio and the importance of sustained collective action toward its complete eradication. The campaign was conceptualized and spearheaded by Service Impact President KD Jamer and Public Image Chair Odessa Balmes, with the billboard artwork designed by Rotary Scholar Christian Alinday. Through the generous support of Julia Ads, facilitated by RCNH member Chu Julia, the club secured the billboard space with the rental fees waived, demonstrating the value of mobilizing community partnerships and professional resources in advancing humanitarian causes. Beyond raising awareness, the advocacy encouraged public participation in Rotary's End Polio Now campaign by promoting individual contributions, community engagement, and continued support for global immunization and disease prevention efforts. Strategically displayed along one of Naga City's major thoroughfares, the billboard sought to extend Rotary's message beyond its membership and inspire the broader public to become active partners in building a polio-free world. Aligned with Rotary's commitment to Disease Prevention and Treatment and the \*Buhay at Kalusugan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the initiative demonstrated how creative communication, volunteer leadership, and private-sector collaboration can amplify the reach of public health advocacy. Through this campaign, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its dedication to protecting future generations from preventable diseases, strengthening public awareness of Rotary's humanitarian mission, and contributing to the global effort to end polio for good.

projects.project_name: RCNH & BIGGS PARTNERSHIP FOR THE DISKWENTULONG CARD
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights strengthened its DiskwenTulong Card (DTC) Program through a strategic partnership with Bigg's Diner, one of Bicol's most established and successful homegrown restaurant chains, expanding the program's network of participating establishments and enhancing its value to cardholders. Formalized through a Memorandum of Agreement signed by Service Impact President KD Jamer and Bigg's President and Chief Executive Officer Carlo Buenaflor, the partnership provides DiskwenTulong Cardholders with an exclusive eight percent (8%) discount at all Bigg's branches throughout the Philippines, effective November 1, 2026. The collaboration represents a significant milestone in the club's efforts to establish sustainable partnerships with private-sector institutions that share its commitment to community development and social responsibility. Through the DiskwenTulong Card Program, the club seeks to integrate practical consumer benefits with its broader service and fundraising objectives, encouraging individuals to support Rotary's humanitarian initiatives while enjoying exclusive privileges from participating businesses. With the card offered at ₱500 and valid until December 31, 2027, the program provides an opportunity to expand community participation and strengthen the club's capacity to mobilize resources for its service projects. Beyond the commercial benefits extended to cardholders, the partnership demonstrates how collaboration between civic organizations and established local enterprises can create mutually beneficial opportunities that promote community engagement, corporate social responsibility, and sustainable service delivery. By welcoming Bigg's into the growing DiskwenTulong Card Network, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced its commitment to innovative fundraising, institutional partnership development, and long-term organizational sustainability. The initiative highlights the club's continuing efforts to transform everyday consumer transactions into opportunities for meaningful community support, strengthen its financial capacity to implement humanitarian programs, and create lasting impact through strategic collaboration with the business sector.

projects.project_name: LIKAY @ NAGA CITY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights implemented LIKAY: The Yield to Pedestrians Road Safety Signage Project in Naga City as part of its continuing commitment to promoting public safety, responsible road use, and the protection of human lives. On October 23, 2026, the club officially turned over reflectorized pedestrian crossing signages to the City Government of Naga, represented by Mayor Leni Robredo and Councilor AReiz Macaraig, to support local efforts toward creating safer and more pedestrian-friendly roads. Bearing the messages “SLOW DOWN,” “PREPARE TO STOP,” and “YIELD TO PEDESTRIANS,” the signages were designed to provide clear and highly visible reminders to motorists approaching pedestrian crossings, particularly during nighttime and low-visibility conditions. The initiative sought to encourage responsible driving behavior, strengthen public awareness of pedestrian rights, and reduce the risk of road accidents involving vulnerable road users, including children, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities. Beyond the installation of physical safety reminders, the project emphasized the importance of mutual respect, patience, discipline, and shared responsibility in maintaining order and preventing avoidable harm on public roads. Through its partnership with the City Government of Naga, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights demonstrated how civic organizations and local government institutions can collaborate in addressing everyday community safety concerns through practical and sustainable interventions. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention, the initiative promoted a culture of respect, consideration, and nonviolence in shared public spaces. By contributing to safer pedestrian crossings and encouraging greater accountability among motorists, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives, strengthening community welfare, and creating lasting impact through meaningful and preventive public safety initiatives.

projects.project_name: END POLIO MOTORCADE @ NAGA CITY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights joined fellow Rotary, Rotaract, and Interact Clubs in Naga City in commemorating World Polio Day on October 24, 2026, through a collaborative End Polio Motorcade and community outreach activity aimed at strengthening public awareness and support for Rotary International's global polio eradication campaign. The motorcade brought together Rotarians, Rotaractors, Interactors, and community volunteers in a unified demonstration of solidarity and commitment to the worldwide effort to eliminate poliomyelitis. Following the motorcade, participants proceeded to Barangay Panicuason, Naga City, where they conducted a Community Walk and Snack activity with local children, providing opportunities for meaningful interaction while reinforcing the importance of protecting future generations from vaccine-preventable diseases. The initiative highlighted the Philippines' certification as polio-free in 2000 and emphasized the continuing need for vigilance, immunization, and international cooperation, particularly as wild poliovirus remains endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Beyond commemorating the progress achieved through decades of vaccination and public health initiatives, the activity sought to inspire greater community involvement in the End Polio Now campaign by encouraging public awareness, volunteer participation, and financial contributions to support vaccination programs, disease surveillance, and other eradication efforts. The collaboration among Rotary's different generations of service organizations demonstrated the strength of collective action in advancing humanitarian causes and sustaining public engagement in global health challenges. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Disease Prevention and Treatment and the \*Buhay at Kalusugan\* pillar of the club's BAKAS thrust, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to promoting preventive healthcare, strengthening partnerships within the Rotary family, and advocating for a future where every child can grow and thrive free from the threat of polio. Through its participation, the club contributed to sustaining the momentum of the global eradication campaign and advancing Rotary's historic mission to end polio for good.

projects.project_name: AI NEXT PHILIPPINES
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated as a Community Partner of AI NEXT PH 2026, recognized as Bicol's First Artificial Intelligence Summit, held on October 27–28, 2026, at Lendes Convention Hall in Naga City. The two-day gathering brought together technology innovators, entrepreneurs, professionals, educators, business leaders, and community stakeholders to promote awareness, knowledge-sharing, and collaboration in the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence. Featuring a keynote address by Naga City Mayor Leni G. Robredo, interactive AI workshops, breakout discussions, and the FutureTech Co-Create Challenge, the summit provided a platform for exploring emerging technologies, developing practical digital competencies, and identifying innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Through its involvement as a Community Partner, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights supported efforts to broaden access to technological knowledge, encourage responsible innovation, and strengthen the readiness of local professionals, businesses, and communities to participate in an increasingly technology-driven economy. The initiative emphasized the importance of digital transformation, lifelong learning, and interdisciplinary collaboration in enhancing professional capabilities, improving productivity, and creating new opportunities for economic and social development. Aligned with Rotary's commitment to Vocational Service, the partnership demonstrated the club's recognition of technology education and innovation as important instruments for professional growth and community empowerment. By supporting a regional platform that connected emerging technologies with practical applications and community needs, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reinforced its commitment to fostering professional excellence, encouraging meaningful collaboration between the technology sector and civic organizations, and contributing to the development of a digitally empowered, innovative, and future-ready Bicol Region.

projects.project_name: PUSONG ORAGON PARA SA PRESONG ORAGON @ BJMP NAGA - FEMALE DORMITORY, DEL ROSARIO, NAGA CITY
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights participated as a partner organization and donor in “Hale sa Pusong Oragon, Para sa Presong Oragon: A Humanitarian Aid Visit to the Bicolano Jail Community,” a comprehensive humanitarian outreach initiative spearheaded by the Alpha Phi Omega (APO) Oragon 185 Metro Naga Alumni Association, Inc., at the BJMP Naga City District Jail Female Dormitory in Barangay Del Rosario, Naga City. Conducted in observance of National Correctional Consciousness Week (NACOCOW) 2026, the project brought together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, civic organizations, and community volunteers to extend essential services and compassionate assistance to 40 female Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs). Representing the Rotary Club of Naga Heights were Service Impact President Atty. KD Jamer and Charter President Atty. Oying Rosales, who volunteered their professional expertise by providing free legal consultations, advice, and guidance concerning pending cases, legal rights, and available legal remedies. In addition to its legal assistance and donor participation, the club supported a multidisciplinary outreach program that provided free medical examinations, health assessments, essential medicines, dental consultations and necessary tooth extractions, personal hygiene kits, and food and nutritional assistance. The initiative also extended educational support through the distribution of school supplies and learning materials for PDLs enrolled in the Alternative Learning System (ALS), alongside clothing, slippers, gifts, and recreational items intended to promote their dignity, comfort, and emotional well-being. Beyond addressing immediate humanitarian needs, the project emphasized the fundamental importance of access to justice, healthcare, education, and humane treatment for individuals under custodial care. Through the voluntary application of legal expertise, the club demonstrated Rotary's commitment to Vocational Service while supporting its areas of focus on Disease Prevention and Treatment, Basic Education and Literacy, and Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention. Aligned with the club's BAKAS thrust, the initiative reinforced the value of professional volunteerism, interorganizational collaboration, and compassionate service in reaching vulnerable and underserved populations. By extending meaningful assistance beyond the barriers of incarceration, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its commitment to upholding human dignity, promoting equitable access to essential services, and creating lasting impact through service that recognizes the inherent worth and rights of every individual.

projects.project_name: PROJECT GIYA @ MILAOR, CAMARINES SUR
projects.description: The Rotary Club of Naga Heights strengthened its commitment to Vocational Service and access to justice through its participation as Co-Presenter of the inaugural Project GIYA, a community-based free legal aid initiative organized by Jamer Law in partnership with the Local Government Unit of Milaor, Camarines Sur. Conducted on October 31, 2026, at the Sangguniang Bayan of Milaor, the project sought to address barriers to legal assistance by bringing essential legal services directly to indigent and underserved members of the community. Through the collective efforts of volunteer lawyers, including Rotarians and non-Rotarians, the activity provided free legal consultations, legal advice, document review, drafting of simple affidavits and basic legal instruments, notarization of simple affidavits, and referrals for matters requiring further legal assistance or representation. The initiative was supported by the Municipal Government of Milaor through Municipal Councilor Hon. Senen Bermas VI, whose collaboration helped facilitate the delivery of legal services to local residents. Beyond providing immediate legal assistance, Project GIYA aimed to promote legal awareness, empower individuals to understand and assert their rights, and encourage the peaceful and lawful resolution of disputes. By mobilizing members of the legal profession to volunteer their knowledge, skills, and expertise for the benefit of the public, the project exemplified Rotary's principle of Vocational Service and demonstrated the important role of professional responsibility in advancing social welfare. Aligned with Rotary's area of focus on Peacebuilding and Conflict Prevention and the club's BAKAS thrust, the initiative highlighted the value of collaboration among legal practitioners, civic organizations, and local government institutions in strengthening access to justice. Through Project GIYA, the Rotary Club of Naga Heights reaffirmed its dedication to promoting equal access to legal assistance, protecting individual rights, strengthening community empowerment, and creating lasting impact by ensuring that the guidance and protection of the law become more accessible to those who need them most.
